How to generate a RESTful API request on Cisco Nexus Dashboard?
Version: 6.3.1
API name: get information of device connector versions

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends an HTTP GET request to retrieve Device Connector Versions information from a specified URL. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. The URL points to a JSON file containing Device Connector Versions information.

params.description: Optional query parameters to include in the GET request as key-value pairs.

message.content:
Below is a step‑by‑step guide on how to generate a **RESTful API request** for the *“Get information of device connector versions”* endpoint in **Cisco Nexus Dashboard 6.3.1**. I’ll cover both the **web UI (API Explorer)** and a **command‑line (cURL)** approach so you can pick whichever fits your workflow. --- ## 1. Using the Cisco Nexus Dashboard API Explorer The API Explorer is a built‑in Swagger‑UI that lets you view all available APIs, fill in parameters, and generate the exact HTTP request you need. | Step | Action | Notes | |------|--------|-------| | **1** | Log in to the Nexus Dashboard web console. | Use your admin credentials. | | **2** | Click the **“Developer”** or **“API Explorer”** tab (the exact label may vary). | This opens the Swagger UI. | | **3** | In the left pane, locate the **“Device Connector”** group. | Expand it to see all related endpoints. | | **4** | Find the endpoint named **“Get information of device connector versions”**. | It will look something like `/api/v1/device-connector/versions`. | | **5** | Click the endpoint to expand its details. | You’ll see the HTTP method (`GET`), required headers, and optional query parameters. | | **6** | Fill in any required parameters (e.g., `deviceId`, `connectorId`). | If none are required, you can skip this step. | | **7** | Click **“Generate Request”** (or “Try it out”). | The UI will automatically build the full request. | | **8** | Click **“Send”** to execute the request. | The response will appear below the request pane. | | **9** | Copy the generated cURL command (if you want to use it elsewhere). | Look for the “cURL” tab or button. | ### Example cURL from the API Explorer ```bash curl -X GET "https:///api/v1/device-connector/versions" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer " \ -H "Accept: application/json" ``` > **Tip:** Replace `` with your actual Nexus Dashboard hostname/IP and `` with a valid OAuth2 bearer token. --- ## 2. Using cURL Directly (Command Line) If you prefer to script or test from the terminal, you can construct the request manually. ### Prerequisites 1. **Authentication Token** – Obtain an OAuth2 bearer token via the `/oauth/token` endpoint or your preferred auth flow. 2. **Endpoint URL** – For version 6.3.1, the base URL is typically `https:///api/v1`. ### Sample Request ```bash #!/usr/bin/env bash # Variables DASHBOARD_HOST="nexus-dashboard.example.com" ACCESS_TOKEN="eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..." # Make the request curl -X GET "https://${DASHBOARD_HOST}/api/v1/device-connector/versions" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \ -H "Accept: application/json" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" ``` ### Expected Response ```json { "status": "success", "data": [ { "connectorId": "conn-123", "version": "v1.2.3", "releaseDate": "2024-01-15" }, ... ] } ``` > **Note:** The exact JSON structure depends on your Nexus Dashboard configuration and the specific API implementation. --- ## 3. Using Python (Optional) If you’d like to integrate this into a Python script, you can use the `requests` library: ```python import requests url = "https://nexus-dashboard.example.com/api/v1/device-connector/versions" headers = { "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN", "Accept": "application/json", "Content-Type": "application/json" } response = requests.get(url, headers=headers) print(response.json()) ``` --- ## 4. Common Pitfalls & Troubleshooting | Issue | Likely Cause | Fix | |-------|--------------|-----| | **401 Unauthorized** | Invalid or expired token | Refresh the token or verify scopes | | **404 Not Found** | Wrong endpoint path | Double‑check the API Explorer for the correct URL | | **500 Internal Server Error** | Backend issue | Check Nexus Dashboard logs or contact support | | **Missing Parameters** | Required query params omitted | Add them via the API Explorer or in your request | --- ## 5. Quick Reference Cheat Sheet | Item | Value | |------|-------| | **Base URL** | `https:///api/v1` | | **Endpoint** | `/device-connector/versions` | | **Method** | `GET` | | **Headers** | `Authorization: Bearer `
`Accept: application/json`
`Content-Type: application/json` | | **Query Params** | (none required for this endpoint) | --- ### Final Thoughts - **API Explorer** is the fastest way to see the exact request format and test it live. - **cURL** or **Python** scripts are great for automation or integration into CI/CD pipelines. - Always keep your **access tokens** secure and rotate them regularly. Let me know if you need help with authentication flows, handling pagination, or integrating this into a larger automation framework!
